questions.question:
Consider the following statements related to Genetics.

1. Genetics is the study of heredity and variation

2. The genetic information lies within the cell nucleus of each living cell in the body. 

3. Proteins are made up of one or more polypeptide chains, each of which is composed of a sequence of amino acids, and the DNA sequence of a gene (through an RNA intermediate) is used to produce a specific amino acid sequence.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2, and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Genetics:**

 
 
• Genetics is the **study of heredity and variation**. ***Hence, Statement 1 is correct**.*
 
• Heredity is a biological process where a parent passes certain genes onto their children or offspring.
 
• Every child inherits genes from both of their biological parents and these genes, in turn, express specific traits.
 
• Some of these traits may be physical for example hair and eye colour and skin colour etc.
 
• On the other hand, some genes may also carry the risk of certain diseases and disorders that may pass on from parents to their offspring.
 
• The **genetic information lies within the cell nucleus** of each living cell in the body. *Hence, Statement 2 is correct.*
 
• The information can be considered to be retained in a book for example.
 
• Part of this book with the genetic information comes from the father while the other part comes from the mother.
 
• Genes generally express their functional effect through the production of proteins, which are complex molecules responsible for most functions in the cell. 
 
• **Proteins are made up of one or more polypeptide chains**, each of which is composed of a sequence of amino acids, and the DNA sequence of a gene (through an RNA intermediate) is used to produce a specific amino acid sequence. *Hence, Statement 3 is correct.*
 
• This process begins with the production of an RNA molecule with a sequence matching the gene's DNA sequence, a process called transcription.

questions.question:
Work done can be ______.

I. zero

II. positive

III. Negative
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__I, II, III__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Work**

 
 
• **​**When the body is really moved a **short distance **in the **direction** of the **applied force**, the force is said to have performed **work**.
 
• Since the body is being displaced by the force of (F), therefore **work done** by the **force **in **displacing **the body **through **a **distance **(S) is given by:
 
• W = vec F · vec s
 
Or, W = FS cos θ

 
 
 
 
• ​When the **force **and **displacement **are **acting **in the **same direction**, the amount of **work done **is **positive**. **Hence**, it satisfies **statement** **I**.
 
• When the **force **and **displacement **are **acting **in **opposing directions**, the **work done **is **negative**. Hence, it satisfies statement II.
 
• When the direction force (**Centripetal force**) and **displacement **are **perpendicular**, **no work** is **done**; however, this is not the case for an object traveling in a **circular motion**. Hence, it satisfies statement III.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of 'number – composition' is correct?

I. Atomic number – number of protons

II. Mass number – Sum of number of neutrons and protons
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• I. The **atomic number of an element is indeed equal to the number of protons in an atom of that element.**

***Hence correct.***

 
• II. The **mass number of an atom is defined as the total number of protons and neutrons (collectively known as nucleons) in an atom.**

*Hence correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **In this example, Carbon has an atomic number of 6, which means it has 6 protons in the nucleus of each of its atoms.**

 
 
• This atomic number defines the element
 
• In other words, any atom with **6 protons is a Carbon atom.**
 
• The mass number of **Carbon is 12, indicating that the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus is 12**.
 
 
• Since we know there are **6 protons (from the atomic number),** this means there must also be **6 neutrons (because 12 total nucleons - 6 protons = 6 neutrons).**

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

1. Warm-blooded animals can remain active in cold environment in which cold-blooded animals can hardly move.

2. Humans are cold blooded animals.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
**Option 1** is correct. 

__
 
• On the basis of regulating one’s internal body temperature, animals are been grouped in two categories – Cold-blooded and Warm-blooded
 
• Cold-blooded are the animals which cannot regulate their internal body temperature according to the required level and they keep on changing their temperature according to the changes in external environment temperature.
 
• Although Warm-blooded animals attempt to keep their internal body temperature maintained and does not change the same along with changes in external environment.
 
• **Humans are warm-blooded, **__with our body temperature averaging around 37 ⁰ C.
 
• Humans can regulate our internal body temperature, independent of environment.

questions.question: An alloy is an example of:
questions.solution:
• An **alloy** is an example of **solid solution**. Examples include steel, brass, bronze, etc.
 
• A combination of metal with other metal or with other element is termed as an alloy.
 
• In addition to solid solution, an alloy can also be a mixture of metallic phases.
 
• A heterogeneous system in which one substance is dispersed as very fine particles in another substance called dispersion medium, is termed as a **colloid**.
 
• A colloidal solution in which the dispersed substance and dispersion medium both are liquid, is termed as the **emulsion**.
 
• A mixture that is non-uniform in composition is termed as the **heterogeneous mixture**.

questions.question:
Valency of an element depends on which of the following?

I. Number of losing electron

II. Number of gaining electron

III. Number of sharing electron
questions.solution:
__Explanation:__

__
 
• Valance Electrons: A valence electron is simply the total number of electrons present in the outermost shell of an atom.
 
• Valency: Valency is the number of** electrons an atom loses, gains or shares**__ with other atoms in order to get a stable configuration.

For example-

Atomic Configuration of Carbon (C ) is ( 6 ) = 2,4

__
 
• The valency of Carbon will be 4 as it needs 4 more electrons to get a stable configuration.
 
• The number of valence electrons in carbon is also four as its outermost shell contains 4 electrons.

Atomic Configuration of Nitrogen N ( 7 ) = 2,5

The valency of nitrogen is 3 as it needs 3 more electrons to complete its octet but the number of valence electrons in nitrogen is 5.

So, 

**It can be losing, gaining or sharing of electrons.**__

questions.question:
Which one of the following statements are correct about sound ?

(A) Sound can travel through all media.

(B) Sound is produced by select few vibrating bodies.

(C) Higher the amplitude of vibration, the louder the sound.

(D) Higher the frequency of vibration, the shriller the sound.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**(A), (C), (D)**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• **(A) Sound can travel through all media:** This **statement is correct.** Sound waves are mechanical waves that can propagate through various media, including solids, liquids, and gases. The specific speed of sound and characteristics of sound waves may vary depending on the medium.
 
• **(B) Sound is produced by select few vibrating bodies.** This **statement is incorrect.** Sound is produced by any vibrating object or body. When an object vibrates, it creates disturbances in the surrounding medium, which propagates as sound waves. These vibrations can be produced by a wide range of objects, from musical instruments to vocal cords to everyday objects.
 
• **(C) Higher the amplitude of vibration, the louder the sound:** This** statement is generally correct.** The amplitude of vibration refers to the maximum displacement or intensity of the vibrating object or source. In the case of sound waves, a higher amplitude results in a louder sound.
 
• This is because a larger amplitude corresponds to a higher energy transfer to the surrounding medium, resulting in a more intense sound.
 
• **(D) Higher the frequency of vibration, the shriller the sound:** This** statement is correct.** The frequency of vibration refers to the number of oscillations or cycles per unit time. In the context of sound, the frequency determines the pitch of the sound.** A higher frequency corresponds to a higher pitch or a "shriller" sound, **while a lower frequency corresponds to a lower pitch or a "deeper" sound.

questions.question:
With reference to Red blood Cells, consider the following statements:

1. Red blood cells are responsible for transporting oxygen from lungs to body tissues and also transport carbon dioxide to your lungs for you to exhale.

2. Like white blood cells, red blood cells can change shape easily.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Red blood cells, also known as erythrocytes**. 
 
• They are **responsible for transporting oxygen from lungs to body’s tissues.**
 
• Your tissues produce energy with the oxygen and release a waste, identified as carbon dioxide.
 
• The red blood cells take the carbon dioxide waste to lungs for to exhale. **Hence statement 1 is correct.**
 
• **Red blood cells are microscopic **and have the shape of a flat disk or doughnut, which is round with an indentation in the center, but it **isn’t hollow**.
 
• **Red blood cells don’t have a nucleus like white blood cells**, allowing them to change shape and move throughout your body easier. **Hence statement 2 is incorrect.**
 
• While red blood cells are flexible and can deform to pass through the narrow capillaries, their ability to change shape is limited compared to white blood cells. White blood cells can undergo more significant shape changes due to their roles in the immune response, including phagocytosis and migration through tissues (diapedesis). Red blood cells, however, primarily change shape to a limited extent to move through narrow spaces but do not exhibit the extensive shape-shifting seen in white blood cells.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true?

**Statement A :**

Variations arising during the process of reproduction can be inherited.

**Statement B :**

Changes in the non-reproductive tissues caused by environmental factors are not inheritable.

options.text: Statement A is true and Statement B is false
Statement B is true and Statement A is false
Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false

questions.solution:
**__Concept:__**

__
 
• A **mutation is a sudden change in the DNA sequence of an organism**.
 
• Hugo De Vries was the first one to study mutations in *Oenothera Lamarckiana*.
 
• Mutations can be harmful, beneficial, or have no effect.
 
• Two major categories of mutations are
 
 
• **germline mutations**
 
• **somatic mutations.**
 
 
 
• Mutations that occur in the germ cells i.e., Germline mutations (that occur in eggs and sperm), are inheritable and can be passed on to offspring.
 
• The somatic mutations (that occur in body cells) are not inheritable and are not passed on to the next generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

**Statement A - **

 
• The variations that occur during the reproduction, they occur in the germ cells.
 
• This is known as **germ line mutation**.
 
• A gene change in a body's reproductive cell (egg or sperm) can become incorporated into the DNA of every cell in the body of the offspring. 
 
• The variations occurring in the germ cells **can be inherited**.
 
• Therefore **statement A is true.**

**Statement B - **

 
• Changes in the **non-reproductive tissues caused by environmental factors** occur in the somatic cells.
 
• This is known as **somatic mutation**.
 
• These changes are **not heritable**.
 
• Somatic mutations can occur in any of the body cells except the germ cells (sperm and egg).
 
• Therefore **statement B is true.**

Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: Regarding Meiosis, which of the statements is incorrect?

options.text: Four haploid cells are formed at the end of Meiosis-II
There are two stages in Meiosis, Meiosis-I and II
DNA replication occurs in S phase of Meiosis-II
Pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination occurs in Meiosis-I

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 3**.

**Solution**

__**Concept:**__

__
 
• The eukaryotic **cell cycle** is divided into two phases: the **Interphase and the M phase**.
 
• M phase or **mitosis** is the phase where actual **cell division** occurs.
 
• **Interphase** is the phase between **two successive mitosis divisions**.

**Explanation:**__

Interphase is divided into three phases; **G₁ phase, S phase, and G₂ phase**.

__
 
• **G₁ Phase**

 
 
• It is the **time period between mitosis and the beginning of DNA replication**.
 
• **DNA does not replicate** in this phase.
 
 
 
• **S phase**
 
 
• It is also known as the **Synthesis phase**.
 
• **DNA replication occurs **in this phase.
 
• Here the **number of DNA** molecules increases by **double fold**.
 
 
 
• **G₂ Phase**
 
 
• In this phase **protein synthesis** occurs.
 
 
 
• Prior to meiosis, the cell goes through an **interphase** period during which it** replicates its chromosomes and checks all of its systems to ensure that it is ready to divide**.
 
• Interphase is a stage before meiosis and hence not a part of **meiosis.**

So, the **correct answer is option 3.**

**Additional Information:**__

 
• The cell division which results in the **production of a haploid set of chromosomes** is called **Meiosis.**
 
• There are two stages in Meiosis; **Meiosis I and Meiosis II**.
 
• The stage between the two meiotic divisions is called interkinesis and is generally short-lived.
 
• There is no replication of DNA during interkinesis. Interkinesis is followed by prophase II, a much simpler prophase than prophase I. 
 
• At the end of **Meiosis II**, **four haploid cells** are formed.
